title: What is machine learning?
author: Naushin Ara
text: Machine Learning (ML) is a field of Artificial Intelligence that focuses on developing systems capable of learning from data, identifying patterns, and continuously improving their performance with minimal human intervention.

title: What is machine learning?
author: Shahid Shakeel
text:
Machine Learning is a subset of Artificial Intelligence that prioritizes the development of algorithms and statistical models. Machine learning algorithms help computers learn from data. Also, the equipped data progresses the work of decision-making and identifying patterns. 📊🔎✍
Machine learning incorporates the imitation of human behaviors and works accordingly without the intervention of a human.
- Supervised Learning, Unsupervised Learning, Reinforcement Learning, etc. are some of the crucial parts of Machine Learning. 👈👈
Now, this subject is practical. That means you have to work practically to learn and implement in real-world situations.
If you are eager to learn Machine Learning, you can pursue courses available online.

Whereas, Udacity’s course teaches about supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, etc. 📚📚

This is a technical subject and you have to learn with projects only. As much as you practice with projects, your professional skills will be enhanced and you will get chances to expand your career further.

Storage and processing advances over the past two decades have made it possible for some innovative machine learning-based systems, such as Netflix's recommendation engine and self-driving cars. Machine learning is a critical component of the rapidly expanding discipline of data science. Algorithms are taught using statistical approaches to produce classifications or predictions and to find critical insights in data mining operations. How machine learning works A Decision Process: Machine learning algorithms are typically used to create a prediction or classification. Your algorithm will generate an estimate about a pattern in the data based on some input data, which can be labeled or unlabeled. An Error Function: An error function evaluates the model's prediction. If there are known instances, an error function can compare to determine the model's accuracy. A Model Optimization Process: If the model can fit the data points in the training set better, weights are modified to narrow the gap between the known example and the model prediction. The algorithm will repeat this "evaluate and optimize" procedure, updating weights autonomously until an accuracy criterion is reached. What is the significance of machine learning? Machine learning is significant because it provides organizations with insights into trends in customer behavior and business operating patterns, as well as assisting in the development of new products. Computers are dumb but very fast at it, running billions Continue Reading Or better question is how is it different from normal computer programs? Computers are dumb. They can take a number from somewhere (a memory) or two and do some basic arithmetic on it and store result somewhere else. They can compare numbers and decide to start executing something else depending on result (an “if this then that” rule). That’s basically all they can do. It takes billions of such small steps to produce the result you see on this screen. It all has to be coded in similar fashion to a cooking recipes - painfully step by step. Computers are dumb but very fast at it, running billions of such small steps per second. Hence, to make anything happen the programmer has to know the ‘algorithm’ to write the recipe. You know the ‘algorithm’ that describes a line? Yes: y=a*x+b so you can draw a line by computing y (height on the screen) for every x (width of the screen) and lit a display pixel at such (x,y) coordinates. You get the idea. Now what if you did not know the algorithm? Say you have some observations about world, perhaps a list of search questions on google that you want to relate to a weather patterns of when they were asked? We do not know the algorithm for this hence we cannot code a program that given a serach query would predict the weather it may be related to. Enter “machine learning”. Imagine you have a magic box: it has input, output and two buttons on top: “good”, “bad”. For each input of <search question> the <weather pattern> appears on output. You then run your data set and for each entry applied to the input you get an output. You decide if the produced output is “good” or “bad” by pressing a button when you compare it with your data. After you have run through the data set, and prompted the box with good or bad buttons, the box “somehow learned” the correct response and now can produce good outputs for any input even for input it never saw before. It will “guess” (predict), in more “educated” manner. The box is a computer with a special, but very generic program that can learn and remember the correlation between input and output given a help from you (or rather the dataset). The key is that it’s a mathematical operation of “correlating” of input (words converted to numbers) to output (in numbers again but for human convenience here converted back to words). That is in short “machine learning”. The result of learning is remembered as a big set of numbers (a matrix) in memory but there is no true “computer algorithm” that was created in the process, as it was the case of “programming the algorithm” above. You can see how it’s very useful in cases where an algorithm is not known.
